title: Read staffing, call summaries and unit response reports
summary: Run staffing and call reports with deliberate date and group scopes, inspect the actual detail tables and timestamp sources, and download a unit-row CSV without treating missing data as zero.
prerequisites: Use an authorized reporting account in a fictional practice department with existing calls and staffing history.
Check the department time zone and choose a deliberate report period; preserve operational data and existing staffing.
Use only fictional training records for practice and share downloaded results with authorized recipients.

practice.title: Choose the report for the question
practice.practice: Open Staffing Report and identify one group with more than one recorded staffing category.

practice.title: Read the member-level staffing evidence
practice.practice: Find Matthew Casey and read his group, both listed roles and staffing level.

practice.title: Define a Call Summary period
practice.practice: Prepare the shown October25–29 period and All Groups, then verify both values before Run Report.

practice.title: Check totals against types and states
practice.practice: Confirm that the displayed Closed and Active counts add to the report total.

practice.title: Understand how calls are assigned to groups
practice.practice: Read the Calls by Group explanation and identify the five calls attributed to Command.

practice.title: Read the individual call rows
practice.practice: Locate the native training call ending0008 and distinguish Open from its N/A on-scene value.

practice.title: Set the Call Unit Times window
practice.practice: Read the Unit Times start and end and identify the thirty-minute difference from the earlier summary.

practice.title: Interpret timestamps and their linkage
practice.practice: Compare a Dispatch only row with a Unit status row without filling any blank timestamp.

practice.title: Download and interpret the real CSV
practice.practice: Download the CSV and compare one DispatchOnly row with the matching report row; retain blank cells.

practice.title: Run an explicit group scope
practice.practice: Run the shown default period with Command and confirm the displayed descendant-group scope.

practice.title: Read yearly, quarterly and monthly tables
practice.practice: Find October’s five calls and explain why the following zero-call months still show YTD5.

practice.title: Change one reporting variable at a time
practice.practice: Compare Command5 and All Groups16 only after confirming the identical displayed start and end.

practice.title: Apply the same checks across departments
practice.practice: Choose one sector example and state the report, period, group scope and missing-data rule you would use.

sector_examples.Chicago Fire: Run a station-scoped call summary for a fixed exercise period, then inspect the matching unit times before describing response totals.
sector_examples.Community care and mental health: Review operational call workload in an agreed period without adding client histories or treating software timestamps as an assessment.
sector_examples.Search and rescue: Compare mission-period call groups using the same boundaries and distinguish missing unit times from recorded zero-duration activity.
sector_examples.Security: Review current recorded staffing and a bounded patrol call period; do not equate the staffing chart with attendance.
sector_examples.Wildland: Compare a defined seasonal window and its group scope; treat partial-period and future zero rows explicitly.
sector_examples.Industrial response: Inspect a training call’s unit-status chronology and preserve missing fields in a CSV used for an internal software exercise.
